title: Refine implicit-surface weights with chain-aware influence domains
description:
## User Mandate

> Sythesize these audits of the skeeltal mesh system and then help improve the bone vertex weights. The feet are also no longer flat on the ground, but that's a seperate issue, I think

STRICT. Reconcile the supplied skeleton audits and improve bone vertex weights without merging the separate foot-grounding issue into this task.

## Summary
Refine the completed MVP segment-distance weighting model for the implicit welded surface so anatomical chains control influence locality at torso, hip, shoulder, mirrored-limb, and neighboring-limb junctions.

## Scope
- Preserve closest-point-on-segment distance, morphology-derived radii, deterministic top-four selection, normalization, mirror behavior, and build-time-only ownership from TSK-0131.
- Add explicit chain or domain metadata supplied by resolved skeleton/rig segmentation. Do not infer part identity from mesh vertices or Unity object order.
- Define controlled cross-domain blending at pelvis/shoulder junctions and reject unrelated neighboring-limb influences outside the configured envelope.
- Add deterministic fixture coverage for hip, shoulder, mirrored limb, branch, knee, and elbow regions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Existing TSK-0131 fixtures remain valid.
- Representative hip and shoulder vertices do not receive unrelated limb-chain influences outside the configured transition domain.
- Joint transition vertices blend only the anatomically adjacent domains and remain normalized with no more than four influences.
- Rest-pose equivalence, known-pose deformation, mirror parity, repeated-generation determinism, and build-time-only weighting remain proven.
- Unity or focused runtime validation records the deformation result on generated geometry.

## Validation
Run focused runtime tests for the weighting fixtures, runtime assembly builds, and Unity PlayMode validation on generated geometry when available. Record any Unity unavailability as a blocker.

## Findings
The current `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring` implementation is a confirmed geometric MVP, not a naive nearest-bone-center implementation. This task is an additive quality refinement and must not duplicate or reopen TSK-0131.

## Blockers
Compact anatomical rig segmentation may be required before domain metadata can be stable. The separate flat-feet/ground-contact issue is out of scope.

## Next Step
Define the domain contract against the current `SkeletonSnapshot` and `ResolvedCreatureSnapshot`, then add one hip and one shoulder discriminator fixture before changing the authoring algorithm.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Round 2 implementation and validation evidence (uncommitted):

Implementation: Added an explicit `InfluenceDomain` contract to `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring` with a stable allowed-domain set per rest vertex. `BoneSegmentInfluence` now carries `DomainId`, sourced from resolved `BoneSnapshot.SourcePartId` (falling back to bone id only when source metadata is empty); legacy constructors remain available. Domain eligibility is applied before the existing closest-point-on-segment falloff, deterministic weight/BoneIndex ranking, top-four selection, and normalization. Added deterministic hip-transition and mirrored-transition fixtures proving unrelated neighboring domains are excluded, adjacent body/hip domains can blend, mirrored domain selection remains deterministic, and <=4 normalized influences remain intact. No skeleton topology, DNA derivation, per-vertex part attribution, pose files, task JSON, editor visualization, compact Body rig, or flat-feet logic was changed.

Focused validation: `dotnet test ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore --filter FullyQualifiedName~ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoringTests` exited 0 and built successfully, but the runner reported no test discovery/execution counts; therefore this is compile evidence, not a verifiable executed test count. After the fixture metadata correction, the same command again exited 0 with no discovery count.

Build validation: `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` exit 0, warnings 0, errors 0. `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` exit 0, warnings 0, errors 0. Targeted `git diff --check -- Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Animation/Binding/ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.cs Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoringTests.cs` exit 0. Global diff check remains blocked by pre-existing trailing whitespace in unrelated `Assets/Test.unity`.

Unity validation: Connected Unity 6000.5.9f1 was available. Refresh/compile request completed and the final console contained zero errors/warnings. Focused EditMode runs by test name and `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime` assembly both returned succeeded with `total: 0, passed: 0, failed: 0`; Unity test discovery is therefore unavailable for this fixture in the current editor state and no Unity test pass is claimed.

Residual risk: Runtime/test source compiles, but the new domain contract has not been executed by the Unity Test Framework in this session because the assembly/test discovery returned zero. The contract is caller-supplied and intentionally does not derive domains from mesh vertices; integration of resolved anatomical domain metadata remains the next boundary. TSK-0148 compact Body segmentation and TSK-0149 visualization remain deferred. Round remains InProgress pending a real focused Unity test run.

Sprint round 2 implementation evidence (uncommitted): added the explicit InfluenceDomain contract and optional DomainId on BoneSegmentInfluence. BuildSegmentInfluences/BuildBindingInfluences source DomainId from resolved BoneSnapshot.SourcePartId with bone ID fallback; Author filters candidates by caller-supplied allowed domains before the existing closest-point-on-segment distance/falloff and deterministic top-four normalization. Legacy constructors and no-domain call sites preserve existing behavior. Added hip transition and mirrored-neighbor deterministic fixtures; existing TSK-0131 fixture source remains intact.

Global diff check remains blocked by pre-existing trailing whitespace in Assets/Test.unity. Evidence confidence: spot-checked source/diff; build report-trusted; runtime behavior unverified.

Non-obvious decisions: SourcePartId is the existing resolved domain identity; filtering is opt-in through the new vertexDomains overload; transition vertices explicitly list adjacent domains; no per-vertex part attribution or DNA derivation was added. Residual risk: caller-supplied domain metadata is not yet integrated with compact anatomical segmentation, and the new fixtures have not executed. Keep TSK-0147 InProgress pending repair of Unity test discovery and focused runtime validation.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Follow-up review from current Unity screenshot/state: confirmed a fundamental mirror-domain identity bug in the round-two implementation. `SkeletonInferrer` emits mirrored and unmirrored bones with the same `SourcePartId = part.Id`; deriving `BoneSegmentInfluence.DomainId` from SourcePartId alone therefore collapses both sides into one weighting domain. Corrected `BuildSegmentInfluences` and `BuildBindingInfluences` to append `SemanticBoneResolver.MirrorSuffix` for mirrored bones, and added `BuildSegmentInfluences_MirroredBonesGetDistinctDomainsFromSameSourcePart` proving identical authored source IDs produce `hip` versus `hip_mirror` and select separate left/right bone indices under explicit vertex domains.

Important live-path finding: source search shows no runtime/editor call site currently consumes `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.Author` or `BuildBindingInfluences`; the domain-aware weighting code is not yet connected to the generated renderer/skinning path. Therefore this correction prevents domain collapse at the authoring seam but does not by itself explain or fix the visible Unity deformation until the binding integration is implemented and validated.

Validation: edited weighting files report no diagnostics; scoped `git diff --check` passed. Runtime and test builds are blocked by a pre-existing unrelated worktree change: `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Morphology/Extraction/DensityGrid.cs` currently lacks `TryEstimateGradient`, while `MarchingCubesExtractor.cs` still calls it. Both `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` and `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` fail at that missing API. Unity bridge was not actually connected in this session despite the editor screenshot; all MCP queries returned `No Unity Editor instances found`, so no live hierarchy or focused test result is claimed.

Residual risk: the screenshot-level mirrored-leg coupling remains unverified and likely requires the missing binding integration plus Unity PlayMode deformation evidence. The separate DensityGrid extraction change is preserved untouched. TSK-0147 remains blocked.
